html:
A world religion founded in the 3rd century CE by the prophet Mani (216 to about 274) in the Sasanian Empire, in what is now Iraq. It spread from Roman North Africa to China.

Mani taught that the world is a battle between two powers, Light and Darkness, good spirit and evil matter. Bits of light are trapped in the material world, and the faithful help free them. He saw himself as the last in a line of prophets after Zoroaster, the Buddha and Jesus. Followers were split into the Elect, who lived strict lives without meat, wine or sex, and the Hearers, who supported them.

Mani wrote his own scriptures and was protected for a time by Shah Shapur I, but under a later shah he was jailed and died. His faith spread west, where Augustine of Hippo was a Hearer for nine years before turning against it, and Rome persecuted it under Diocletian. It spread east along the Silk Road. The Uyghur Khaganate made it its state religion in 763, and it lasted in southern China into the Ming era. "Manichaean" still means seeing the world in black and white.
